claims.text: Substituting constituent elements with elements of more similar atomic radii will reduce local lattice distortions in the high-entropy alloy.
Reducing local lattice distortions will enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling will increase the superconducting transition temperature.
The proposed starting material is a fully disordered, single-phase alloy containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each.
A wide disparity in constituent atomic radii induces significant local lattice distortions in the starting material.
The modified alloy will replace one or more constituents with alternatives having closer atomic radii while retaining the overall electron count and structural phase.
The baseline and modified samples are to remain single-phase solid solutions and be processed with the same annealing time and cooling rate.
Atomic-radius mismatches among constituent elements are the origin of the relevant local lattice distortions.
Reducing atomic-radius mismatch produces less perturbed phonon modes.
Less perturbed phonon modes enhance the coherence of electron–phonon coupling.
Electron–phonon coupling is responsible for superconductivity in the proposed alloy.
The modified alloy should have a higher superconducting transition temperature than the baseline.
The modified alloy should show reduced lattice strain by X-ray diffraction peak broadening, pair-distribution-function analysis, or Raman spectroscopy.
The modified alloy should show a more coherent phonon spectrum.
The proposed mechanism is limited to disordered, single-phase high-entropy alloys whose superconductivity is primarily mediated by electron–phonon interactions.
Dominant additional scattering mechanisms or phase separation may invalidate the proposed relationship.
